userStories.title: MemoryFlushCallback - Agent-driven memory reflection
userStories.description: As a system operator, I want a callback that periodically prompts the agent to reflect and save observations to memory, and auto-appends a run summary at end. The agent decides what to write (agent-driven); the callback decides when to prompt (system-driven).
acceptanceCriteria: memory/callback.py exists with MemoryFlushCallback extending AsyncCallbackHandler
Constructor accepts MemoryStore, flush_interval (default 20), and task_description
on_llm_start: every flush_interval steps, appends a memory reflection system message to messages list prompting the agent to save observations
Reflection prompt references memory tools (memory_search, memory_get) and instructs agent to save failed strategies, discoveries, state observations
on_run_end: auto-appends structured run summary (task, steps, tokens, outcome) to daily log via MemoryStore
Does not crash if memory_logs/ directory does not exist (creates it)
memory/__init__.py exports MemoryFlushCallback
agenthle_agent.py instantiates MemoryFlushCallback and passes it in ComputerAgent callbacks= list
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_callback.py passes
run_magic_tower.sh completes and memory_data/memory_logs/ contains daily log with auto-summary entry from on_run_end
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
userStories.notes: Depends on US-MEM-002/003 for the agent to actually write via tools. Without tools, the reflection prompt is injected but agent can only acknowledge it.

userStories.title: Upgrade memory_search to semantic/vector search
userStories.description: As an agent, I want memory_search to use embedding-based semantic search so I can find conceptually related memories even when exact keywords don't match (e.g., searching 'stuck' finds 'blocked', searching 'floor 3' finds 'third level'). This upgrades the current keyword substring matching to vector similarity, following OpenClaw's approach but keeping TinyClaw's simplicity.
acceptanceCriteria: MemoryStore.search() supports a backend parameter: 'keyword' (current default) or 'semantic'
Semantic backend embeds query and memory lines using a configurable embedding model (default: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small or a local model)
Embedding index is built lazily on first semantic search and refreshed when files change (mtime check)
memory_search tool gains optional 'mode' parameter: 'keyword', 'semantic', or 'auto' (default 'auto' which falls back to keyword if embeddings unavailable)
Optional 'min_score' parameter for semantic mode to filter low-relevance results
Graceful degradation: if embedding API is unavailable or OPENAI_API_KEY not set, falls back to keyword search with a warning in results
No new required dependencies — embedding support is optional (guard imports with try/except)
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_search_semantic.py passes (tests: semantic finds synonyms keyword misses, fallback to keyword on missing API key, min_score filtering, index refresh on file change)
run_magic_tower.sh works with both modes (keyword default still works, semantic opt-in via env var)
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
userStories.notes: Upgrade path from keyword to semantic search. Trigger conditions: memory corpus grows large, cross-task memory needed, or agent recall drops due to vocabulary mismatch. OpenClaw uses embedding providers with fallback; TinyClaw should keep it simpler with a single optional embedding backend. Consider local embeddings (e.g., sentence-transformers) to avoid API cost.
